subject: Galceran et al. (2004)
object: Galceran et al. (2004) showed that in mice, a targeted mutation of Lef1 affected the patterning of somites and the expression of components of the Notch pathway. The mutation abrogated LEF1 function and impaired the activity of coexpressed TCF factors.

subject: Galceran et al. (2004)
object: Galceran et al. (2004) found that LEF1 bound multiple sites in the Dll1 promoter both in vitro and in vivo. Mutating these LEF1-binding sites impaired expression of a Dll1-LacZ transgene in the presomitic mesoderm. Induced expression of LEF1-beta-catenin activated endogenous Dll1 expression in fibroblastic cells. The authors concluded that Wnt signaling can affect the Notch pathway through LEF1-mediated regulation of Dll1.

subject: Lévy et al. (2020)
object: Lévy et al. (2020) reported 2 unrelated patients with severe oligodontia affecting both primary and permanent teeth, hypotrichosis and hypohidrosis, consistent with hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia. Both patients also had taurodontism and a particular alveolar bone defect.

subject: Lévy et al. (2020)
object: In 2 unrelated patients with hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia, Lévy et al. (2020) identified de novo deletions at chromosome 4q25 that included the LEF1 gene. The authors concluded that the findings provided further evidence that LEF1 haploinsufficiency causes ectodermal dysplasia. They noted that no pathogenic variants involving LEF1 had previously been reported in humans.

subject: LEF1 4q25 de novo deletion encompassing LEF1
Lévy et al. (2020)
object: Lévy et al. (2020) noted that, in mice, targeted inactivation of the Lef1 gene completely blocks the development of multiple ectodermal appendages.

subject: Dufour et al. (2022)
object: Dufour et al. (2022) concluded that monoallelic and biallelic variants in LEF1, which encodes a transcription factor acting downstream of the WNT-beta-catenin signaling pathway, cause a novel syndrome of limb malformations and ectodermal dysplasia.

subject: Dufour et al. (2022)
object: Dufour et al. (2022) reported 12 individuals with LEF1 variants: 11 from 4 unrelated families and 1 from a consanguineous family. The phenotypic spectrum included ectodermal dysplasia and various limb malformations, such as radial ray defects, polydactyly, or split hand/foot.

subject: Dufour et al. (2022)
object: Dufour et al. (2022) stated that, depending on the type and location of the LEF1 variant, this condition can be inherited in either an autosomal dominant or an autosomal recessive manner.

subject: Dufour et al. (2022)
object: Using high-throughput sequencing, Dufour et al. (2022) found monoallelic LEF1 variants in 11 affected individuals from 4 unrelated families. They also found a biallelic LEF1 variant in an affected individual from a consanguineous family. Earlier, LEF1 had been suspected as a candidate gene for ectodermal dysplasia in 2 individuals with 4q35 microdeletions.

subject: Dufour et al. (2022)
object: Functional studies by Dufour et al. (2022) used immunofluorescence, immunoblotting, pulldown assays, and RNA sequencing. The authors suggested 2 molecular mechanisms. Haploinsufficiency or loss of DNA binding was responsible for a mild to moderate phenotype, whereas loss of beta-catenin binding caused by biallelic variants was associated with a severe phenotype.

subject: Dufour et al. (2022)
object: Transcriptomic studies by Dufour et al. (2022) showed altered WNT signaling associated with the LEF1 variants.

subject: Hassan et al. (2024)
object: Hassan et al. (2024) reported a family with hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia, which they considered to expand the spectrum of LEF1-related disorders.
